Empaques Universal SA Faces Insolvency, Halting Operations in Costa Rica

San José—Empaques Universal SA, a major player in Costa Rica’s chemicals packaging sector, has entered insolvency proceedings, resulting in a suspension of core manufacturing and delivery operations, company officials confirmed Thursday. The process, which began earlier this week, follows months of declining cash flow and mounting liabilities amid sluggish demand in regional markets.

“Our immediate focus is to safeguard what we can of the business and to protect our workforce,” said interim CEO Luis Ramírez in a press statement. “We are engaging with creditors and exploring all legal avenues, but at this stage, production is on hold and new orders cannot be fulfilled.”

Empaques Universal SA, founded in 1992, employs nearly 150 workers at its main facility in Cartago. The company specializes in industrial packaging solutions for a range of chemical producers across Central America. As insolvency proceedings unfold, workers have been asked not to report to the plant, with wages for the current pay period still under review.

Trade unions expressed concern over the welfare of employees. “This situation puts dozens of families in jeopardy,” said Rosa Quesada of the National Chemical Workers Union. “We urge authorities to ensure a transparent process and to prioritize workers’ rights.”

Local analysts estimate that the company’s bankruptcy could disrupt supply chains for several downstream manufacturers in the region. “Empaques Universal SA’s insolvency is a blow to the chemicals sector and could have a ripple effect,” said Felipe Vargas, an industry consultant.

The insolvency process is ongoing, with further developments expected in the coming weeks.
